name: nds_wifi
statement: The ARM7's wireless hardware (0x04800000-0x0480FFFF: 16-bit registers at 0x04808000, 8 KiB of Wi-Fi RAM at 0x04804000), as far as a game's wireless driver needs it to come up and stay idle: the register file; the baseband chip's registers behind W_BB_CNT (5xxxh writes W_BB_WRITE, 6xxxh latches the register for W_BB_READ; the fixed ones stay fixed); the RF chip's behind W_RF_DATA2/W_RF_DATA1; power-up (W_POWERSTATE bit 1, W_POWERFORCE, or W_MODE_RST enabled with W_POWER_US bit 1) that completes after wake_microseconds with W_POWERSTATE clear and the RF wake-up interrupt; the microsecond counter (W_US_COUNT, enabled by W_US_COUNTCNT) with the compare (beacon timeslot) interrupt at W_US_COMPARE, the beacon count and the pre- and post-beacon interrupts; W_RANDOM; the RX and TX buffer ports into the Wi-Fi RAM; and TX requests for the LOC1-LOC3 slots that complete after tx_microseconds with their status written. W_IF & W_IE drive the ARM7's Wi-Fi interrupt (IE/IF bit 24).

baseband.fixed_note: pairs of register number and its fixed value (the chip ID 6Dh at 00h); registers 69h-FFh read 0

registers.name: W_ID
registers.bits: chip ID (1440h on the original DS)

registers.name: W_IF
registers.bits: interrupt flags (write 1 to clear): 0 RX done, 1 TX done, 7 TX start, 8 TX buffer count, 9 RX buffer count, 11 RF wake-up, 13 post-beacon, 14 beacon timeslot, 15 pre-beacon

registers.name: W_POWER_US
registers.bits: 0 hold the radio down, 1 power up when W_MODE_RST is enabled

registers.name: W_POWERSTATE
registers.bits: 1 request power-up, 8 waking up, 9 powered down

registers.name: W_RXBUF_*
registers.bits: the RX ring in Wi-Fi RAM and its read port (0x060)

registers.name: W_TXBUF_*
registers.bits: the TX write port (0x070) into Wi-Fi RAM

registers.name: W_US_COMPARE, W_US_COUNT
registers.bits: 64-bit microsecond counter and its compare (units of 1024)

limits: nothing is ever received (no other console, no access point); transmitted frames go nowhere and always succeed; timing is by microsecond, not by bit; the baseband and RF chips are never busy; multiplayer command slots, WEP, the content-free and listen periods, and power-saving sleep after the beacon are not modelled
sources: GBATEK (DS Wifi: I/O map, interrupts, power-down, microsecond timers, baseband and RF chips, TX/RX buffers)
